headline: Memory-efficient alignment and automated pipelines for large sequence collections
label: Scalable Sequence Analysis Tools
summary: Growing genome collections demand alignment and analysis tools that scale in memory and automation, as shown by XTree, CGAS, MAGUS and ZSeekerDB.
synthesis: The common thread is tooling that makes large or heterogeneous sequence collections tractable through automation and modular design. XTree addresses memory cost directly, using k-mer-based alignment against databases of millions of genomes and benchmarked on short and long reads. CGAS integrates nine modules for comparative chloroplast genomics in an automated Python pipeline, spanning gene content, codon usage, SNPs and SSRs. MAGUS applies modular iterative assembly and filtering to eukaryote-dominated pan-domain metagenomes, resolving host, algal, bacterial and viral components. ZSeekerDB differs in kind: it is a resource rather than a search method, cataloguing over 850 million putative Z-forming loci from more than 280,000 genome assemblies with coordinates, Z-scores and taxonomy. What is new is memory-efficient alignment at million-genome scale, alongside a large catalogue of Z-nucleic acid sequences.
